actions.body:
Recent studies in sports psychology explore how reliance on AI-generated training recommendations interacts with athlete autonomy. Drawing on cognitive offloading theory, researchers collected questionnaire data from athletes and found serial associations linking AI dependence to body signal outsourcing, reduced self-regulation, and increased hesitation. While these tools enhance scientific rigor, understanding their psychological trade-offs is crucial for maintaining athlete self-reliance.

Summary
AI training tools can help structure workouts, but heavy reliance on them may cause athletes to ignore their own bodily signals, leading to reduced self-confidence in training decisions.
actions.lede: As athletes increasingly rely on automated training apps, researchers are examining whether outsourcing body signals reduces self-regulation and decision-making confidence.
actions.reason: Publishing an accessible blog post summarizing the completed notebook findings on AI dependence and athlete autonomy.
actions.title: How AI Training Recommendations Shape Athlete Autonomy

review.alternative: Athletes who already outsource bodily signals may naturally seek out AI tools that match their existing preferences.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal experimental data showing that reduced AI reliance reverses body signal outsourcing.

claims.statement: AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing tendency in athletes.

support.explanation: The source demonstrates a direct positive association between reliance on AI training recommendations and outsourcing internal bodily signals.
support.passage: AI training recommendation dependence was significantly and positively associated with body signal outsourcing tendency

review.alternative: Decision hesitation could stem from general competitive anxiety rather than AI tool dependence specifically.
review.would_change_mind: Controlled studies isolating AI feedback from general coaching feedback.

claims.statement: Body signal outsourcing links to a reduced sense of self-regulation and increased training decision hesitation.

support.explanation: The study's structural equation modeling links outsourcing to lower self-regulation and increased hesitation.
support.passage: body signal outsourcing tendency, which was, in turn, positively associated with a reduced sense of self-regulation. A reduced sense of self-regulation was positively associated with training decision hesitation

actions.limitations: The findings are derived from cross-sectional questionnaire data, meaning causal directions remain provisional and require longitudinal tracking.
actions.next_questions: What are the longitudinal impacts of sustained AI training recommendation dependence on long-term athlete autonomy and self-regulation?
